conventions.convention: Comparisons use integer s ≥ 5, J = [0,T] with finite T > 0, the 2π-periodic three-torus, and one fixed coefficient family, coordinate gauge, reconstruction rule and matter branch. Sobolev norms do not quotient by diffeomorphisms.
Compact state sets satisfy K0 ⊂ int K1 ⊂ int K2 ⊂ O. The time matrix has uniform positive lower and finite upper bounds on K2; state H^s and time-derivative H^{s-1} bounds are separate.

For the SI interpretation x0 = c t_phys is a length coordinate and spatial coordinates are dimensionless angles. State components are divided by fixed unit scales before numerical Sobolev norms are formed.
The pullback is (Φ*g)p(X,Y) = gΦ(p)(dΦp X,dΦp Y), for a smooth diffeomorphism Φ.

The stability theorem assumes Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Its Einstein clause uses K_ext(V,W) = g(∇V n,W), complete constrained matter data, harmonic initialization, auxiliary compatibility and conserved reconstructed stress.

Geodesic comparison uses a common compact parameter interval and compact position-velocity set in one chart. Proper-time comparison uses signature (-,+,+,+), a common time orientation, c > 0 and a uniform strictly timelike margin.
The scalar growth example uses dimensionless time and is a general symmetric-hyperbolic illustration, with no asserted Einstein interpretation.

load_bearing.statement: Under the stated choice assumptions and fixed finite-slab comparison context, classical forced solutions satisfy ||u(t)-v(t)||_{H^{s-1}} ≤ exp(λt)(C0||u(0)-v(0)||_{H^{s-1}} + CF∫0^t||Fu(r)-Fv(r)||_{H^{s-1}}dr). Constants depend only on the listed coefficient, compact-state, positivity, regularity and slab data. A smooth unforced reference solution has an H^s neighborhood of smooth admissible initial data whose solutions cover the same slab with common bounds. The separate Einstein reconstruction conclusion requires all stated constrained-data, gauge, compatibility, conservation and persistence hypotheses.

A fixed-gauge finite-slab comparison context fixes the periodic symmetric-hyperbolic coefficient family, gauge and reconstruction, nested compact state sets, positive time-matrix bounds, and separate uniform H^s state and H^{s-1} time-derivative bounds. Compared states use the same coordinate grid and matter branch.

For the stated common unforced reduction, compact state range and uniform state/time-derivative bounds, initial convergence in H^{s-1} gives C^1 convergence of metric components on the fixed slab. Geodesics with convergent initial position-velocity data and lifts retained in the stated common compact chart set converge in C^1. With the additional common orientation, c and uniform timelike margin, their proper times converge.
The pullback tensor Φ*g is defined by (Φ*g)p(X,Y) := gΦ(p)(dΦp X,dΦp Y), for X,Y ∈ TpM.
